newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke says creative accounting for EMU damaging.
newsitem.headline: Welteke says creative accounting for EMU damaging.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke told a conference on monetary union on Monday that creative accounting by European Union member states aimed at meeting the Maastricht criteria was annoying and damaging.

Asked in a Reuters Financial Television interview whether Germany was conducting creating accounting, he replied: "Maybe. I don't blame Germany but I think we should be very careful about blaming others."

He said that in the discussion about France's use of privatisation proceeds from France Telecom and Italy's "euro-tax," Germany had to remember it was also transferring its remaining stake in national airline Lufthansa AG to the private sector.
He also said Germany had made attempts to delay interest payments into 1998 through the issue of zero coupon bonds.

"All the member states have to see how they can fulfill the criteria," he said. States were busy harmonising their statistics and this process could give rise to "rumours and interpretation," he noted.
